# MCQ + NN Forward + Coding + ML Implementations)

[← Pinterest](../README.md) · [Every Pinterest question](../../pinterest.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/mle-intern-codesignal-oa)

`classification` `ml-knowledge` `python`

---

## Requirements

- **MCQ section** — conceptual questions on classification measures (TP/FP, precision/recall, and interpreting confusion-matrix tables), ensemble techniques and interpretability, identifying overfitting (high training performance / low test performance), families of classification losses (cross-entropy and related losses), and why model parameters can become zero (L1 / regularization).
- **Neural-network forward pass** — using supplied weights and an input, manually calculate the output of a small network that includes a sigmoid. There are numerous intermediate sigmoid calculations, so you cannot reliably do them all mentally.
- **LeetCode-style coding** — for a sliding window of size `k`, decide whether the window is "monotonic from the center" (the value at the current position is locally extremal — decreasing on both its left and right).
- **Bootstrap tree** — tree code is supplied; write the bootstrap-resampling and prediction-combination sections. NumPy is unavailable — use only pure-Python `random`.
- **Naive Bayes** — code the standard formulas (prior, likelihood for each feature, and posterior argmax); the data is supplied.
- **Gradient descent** — complete the part of a supplied training-loop template that calculates gradients and updates parameters.

## Notes

- The webcam remains enabled. The platform disallows physical books and second monitors, though a notebook for calculations is allowed — and needed for the NN forward pass. Prepare it before beginning.
- The bootstrap-tree task with NumPy disabled is the most distinctive restriction — practice sampling with `random.choices` from a Python list and converting a prediction list into a majority vote without `numpy.bincount`.
- The naive Bayes exercise is entirely formula-driven — use log space for the products to prevent underflow, add across features, and select the class with the largest value.
- The sliding-window monotonicity task uses unusual wording. Establish what "monotonic from the center" means before writing code — candidates read it as "the center is locally extremal," but the prompt can be interpreted in other ways.
- The precise problem mix and tools vary by sitting: some OAs turn off NumPy for the ML-implementation questions (a pure-Python bootstrap tree), while others allow it (naive Bayes prior/posterior and gradient-descent completion). Check the NumPy rule for each problem in the instructions before coding. The OA lasts 70 minutes and contains approximately 10 problems.

## Preparation

- Arrange paper, a pen, and a basic calculator before opening the OA. The webcam will capture everything, and these items are permitted.
- Practice completing a bootstrap-sampling pass from scratch without NumPy — this is the likeliest place to spend too much time.
- Review the closed-form decision-tree code (gini, information gain) so you can follow the supplied scaffold instead of reconstructing it under time pressure.
- Work through one naive-Bayes example using Iris or a comparable toy dataset; the implementation is brief but easy to mix up when rushed.
